name: APEX-Accounting (public 10-task dev set, tabular + Harbor delivery)

Mercor-Intelligence/archipelago.note: reference only, README was not read

license: CC BY 4.0 (both HF repos, card metadata license: cc-by-4.0; source repo README: 'released under CC BY 4.0, comprising prompts, rubrics, golden responses, task metadata, and the world's source files'). The bundled agent dir has its own LICENSE file, not read.

access.scored_benchmark: closed. README: 'The 160-task scored benchmark is closed. Leaderboard evals can be run for any frontier model on request via apex@mercor.com.'

configs_splits.mercor/apex-accounting-harbor: not a tabular dataset. datasets-server returns 'No (supported) data files found'. 232 files: 10 Harbor task dirs under tasks/, 1 world seed under worlds/, 3 image archives under environment/, agent/ , manifest.json, registry.json, run_task.sh

task_count.private_scored_source: owner statement in both READMEs, not independently verifiable

agent_visible_inputs: source repo: `prompt` field only, plus world/filesystem/** mounted flat at root and that task's task_files/<task>/**. world/apps_data/quickbooks/** is meant to be reached through a tool layer that is NOT in the release (static exports only).

harbor: tasks/<slug>/instruction.md, tasks/<slug>/environment/** (docker-compose.yaml, task_files/filesystem/*, task_files/.harbor/mcp_config.json), world reached only over MCP (Filesystem, Spreadsheets, PDFs, Mail, Code Execution servers rooted at /filesystem), QuickBooks exports seeded to /.apps_data/quickbooks
README field table marks task_id, context_files, rubric, gold_output, metadata as NOT visible to the model
private_material: mercor/apex-accounting: data/dev.jsonl (columns rubric, gold_output, context_files, metadata)
mercor/apex-accounting: tasks/*.json (same 10 records formatted per task, includes rubric + gold_output)
harbor: tasks/*/solution/** (answer.txt, oracle.py, solve.sh, instruction.md)
harbor: tasks/*/tests/** (golden_reference.txt, golden_responses.json, grading_config.json which holds every rubric criterion with acceptable values, grade.py, atif.py, test.sh, Dockerfile)
harbor: tasks/*/mercor.json and tasks/*/agent.json (contents not inspected, treat as private until read)
harbor: environment/apex-verifier/image.tar.gz (grading runner lives at /app/grading inside it)
both READMEs themselves quote nothing answer-bearing, but the source README lists per-model dev scores
native_metric: Leaderboard headline: 'Mean Criteria@3, the percentage of rubric criteria met, averaged over 3 runs per task'. Rubric criteria are binary, unweighted, outcome-based, graded on the final console message only (never the trajectory). Harbor packaging: per-trial reward = `final_score` emitted by the Archipelago grading runner, written to /logs/verifier/reward.txt and reward.json, with per-verifier (per-criterion) scores alongside. How final_score aggregates criteria is inside the verifier image and was NOT verified (expected: fraction of criteria met).

scorer.leaderboard: LM judge DeepSeek-v4-Flash at temperature 0.1 with a GEPA-optimized grading template that is NOT released. One criterion at a time, inputs: task prompt + criterion text + model final output, returns binary Met / Not Met.
scorer.harbor_public: tasks/<slug>/tests/test.sh -> python3 /tests/grade.py in a separate verifier container (apex-verifier:v1). Default judge `vertex_ai/gemini-3-flash-preview` from grading_config.json, override with env GRADING_MODEL. Needs judge credentials (Vertex / LiteLLM proxy / OpenAI / Anthropic / Google / Fireworks env vars are passed through).
scorer.comparability: README: 'Dev-set results are not comparable to leaderboard results and should not be reported as APEX-Accounting scores.'

setup_commands:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("mercor/apex-accounting", split="dev")

hf download mercor/apex-accounting-harbor \
  --repo-type dataset \
  --local-dir apex-accounting-harbor

bash apex-accounting-harbor/environment/load_images.sh
submission_rules: No public submission path. Closed benchmark, leaderboard evals on request via apex@mercor.com. Leaderboard run limits: max 500 steps and 5 million tokens per task, one extra turn to submit on hitting a limit, failing to submit scores zero.

claim_checks.note: datasets-server /size: default/dev num_rows=10. Harbor repo has exactly 10 task dirs (world-9-task-4,5,6,7,13,14,17,23,26,30).
Stated by owner in both READMEs ('160 tasks across 10 held-out worlds', never released). Cannot be independently verified since it is closed.

README `uv tool install harbor==0.20.0`, manifest.json harbor_version 0.20.0, and run_task.sh hard-fails unless `harbor --version` is 0.20.0. PyPI `harbor` latest is 0.23.0, 0.20.0 exists (uploaded 2026-07-18).

File exists (1512 bytes). Requires docker, sha256sum, python3. Verifies archive SHA-256 and image ID, supports `--restore`. Loads 3 linux/amd64 images: apex-world:v1 (3,667,915,127 B), apex-agent:v1 (746,160,102 B), apex-verifier:v1 (574,439,578 B), about 4.99 GB total.

claim_checks.claim: native score is a rubric score
claim_checks.note: Binary rubric criteria judged by an LLM. Caveat: the public Harbor grader uses a different judge (gemini-3-flash-preview) and not the unreleased leaderboard template, so local numbers are a rubric score but not THE leaderboard score.

notes: Harbor README: 'Three rubric criteria were tightened since the tabular release (tasks 4, 5, and 7); everything else is byte-identical.' The two repos therefore disagree on 3 criteria, pick one as the registry source of truth.
Platform is linux/amd64 only. On Apple Silicon this means emulation. Not tested.
Harbor repo was created 2026-09-14 and last modified 2026-09-17, so it is 2 to 5 days old. Expect churn, pin the sha.
Dev world is 'the easiest of the 11 qualifying worlds', dev scores run up to about +14 points over held-out.
Task verifier and agent envs use network_mode = public per task.toml.
Agent timeout 11700 s, verifier timeout 3600 s per task.toml.

name: DABstep (Data Agent Benchmark for Multi-step Reasoning)

adyen/DABstep (dataset).warning: HEAD moves on every leaderboard submission (the Space uploads data/submissions/*.jsonl and data/task_scores/*.jsonl into this same repo). 5 commits landed within 20 minutes on 2026-09-19. Always load with revision= pinned.

license: CC BY 4.0 (dataset card license: cc-by-4.0, Space README license: cc-by-4.0)
access: public, gated=false, private=false. Space runtime stage RUNNING, https://adyen-dabstep.hf.space/ returned HTTP 200.
agent_visible_inputs: tasks config columns task_id, question, guidelines, level (the `answer` column is an empty string in the 3 default-split rows I sampled, I did not scan all 450)
data/context/: acquirer_countries.csv, fees.json, manual.md, merchant_category_codes.csv, merchant_data.json, payments-readme.md, payments.csv
private_material: data/tasks/dev.jsonl `answer` column (10 gold answers, e.g. task 5)

config `task_scores` (public!): columns submission_id, task_id, score(bool), level, agent_answer. Any row with score=True is effectively a gold answer for a hidden task. 1.01M rows. Must never be reachable by the agent.
config `submissions` (public!): task_id, agent_answer, reasoning_trace and metadata for every leaderboard entry. Same leak risk when joined with task_scores.
Space repo: dabstep_benchmark/evaluation/scorer.py and tests/test_scorer.py (scoring logic, not answers, but keep out of agent context)
Gold answers for the 450 default tasks are not in the public dataset files (held server-side by the Space)
native_metric: Accuracy. 'Scores are expressed as the percentage of correct answers.' Tasks carry level easy|hard. 'evaluation is done via quasi exact match between a model's answer and the ground truth (up to some normalization that is tied to the "type" of the ground truth).'
scorer: https://huggingface.co/spaces/adyen/DABstep/blob/main/dabstep_benchmark/evaluation/scorer.py, function question_scorer(input1, input2) -> bool. Numeric: math.isclose(rel_tol=1e-4, abs_tol=1e-4). Lists: compare_lists. Strings: normalized compare, word-subset match, or difflib SequenceMatcher ratio > 0.95. Official scoring of the 450 hidden tasks only happens server-side on submission.
setup_commands:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("adyen/DABstep", name="tasks", split="default")

export MODEL_ID=openai/o3-mini
export API_KEY=<your_api_key>

python3.10 -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate
pip3.10 install -r baseline/requirements.txt

submission_rules.format: JSON Lines. Mandatory fields `task_id` and `agent_answer`, optional `reasoning_trace`. Exact documented example: {"task_id": "task_id_1", "agent_answer": "Answer 1 from your agent", "reasoning_trace": "The different steps by which your model reached answer 1"}
submission_rules.validation_in_code: Any other column is rejected ('Unexpected columns'), NaN rejected, all columns must be strings. Form also requires agent name, model family, organisation, email (repo URL optional, must be https if given). Names limited to [a-zA-Z0-9 _.-]. An organisation+agent_name pair can only be submitted once. Requires Hugging Face OAuth login (hf_oauth: true, gr.LoginButton).
submission_rules.side_effect: A submission is published permanently into the public dataset repo (answers, reasoning_trace, org, HF username). Per my task constraints nothing was submitted.
submission_rules.status: As of Space commit 2026-07-22: 'Validation requests are closed. With DABStep-v2 launching in the coming weeks, we are no longer accepting new validation requests. The Validated Leaderboard is now closed to new entries; previously validated submissions remain as-is. The Unvalidated Leaderboard remains open, you can still submit and receive a score.' Submissions were still landing on 2026-09-19.

claim_checks.note: datasets-server /size: tasks/default num_rows=450. Space copy still says '~450'.
README verbatim: load_dataset("adyen/DABstep", name="tasks", split="default"). Add revision=<sha> yourself, HEAD is unstable.

claim_checks.claim: a dev split exists with answers
claim_checks.note: tasks/dev has 10 rows and the `answer` column is populated (sampled rows: 'NL', 'B. BE').

claim_checks.claim: submission format JSONL with task_id and agent_answer
claim_checks.note: Plus optional reasoning_trace, and nothing else is allowed.
Unvalidated leaderboard open and active. Validated leaderboard closed to new entries since 2026-07-22. DABStep-v2 announced as coming, no v2 dataset verified.

notes: Space copy links to old names adyen/data-agents-benchmark (dataset and space). Both 307-redirect to adyen/DABstep.
Dataset README calls configs 'splits' ('This Dataset has 3 splits: tasks, submissions, task_scores'). They are configs.
Do not load the submissions/task_scores configs for anything agent-facing, and they are 1.3 GB + 147 MB parquet.

name: Finance Agent Benchmark v2 (FABv2)
license: Harness repo + the 27 public samples in it: MIT (GitHub license API + LICENSE file). Private Validation set: 'available for license', terms not public (null). Test set: private.

access.public: 27 samples in data/public.csv and data/public.txt, public GitHub repo
access.private_validation: 450 samples, license from Vals AI on request
access.test: 450 samples, private, all published results are on this split
access.platform: gated, requires approval and company email

agent_visible_inputs: data/public.txt (one question per line) or the `Question` column
Tools in code: calculator, web_search (Tavily), edgar_search (sec-api.io), parse_html_page, price_history (Tiingo), retrieve_information, submit_final_result. Live network, not hermetic.
private_material: data/public.csv `Rubric` column: JSON list of {operator: 'finance_agent_v2_operator', criteria, modifiers: {severity: 1.0|2.0|3.0, category?: 'must_pass'}}. In the 27 samples: 239 checks, severity 1.0 x170, 2.0 x60, 3.0 x9, category must_pass on 79.
`Question Type`, `Expert time (mins)` metadata
There is no Answer column in v2 public.csv, the rubric is the only gold material
native_metric: Page verbatim: 'Partial Credit (primary): the dealbreaker-gated, severity-weighted average of per-check scores. A response with a correct dealbreaker but a few peripheral misses scores below 100%; a response with any failed dealbreaker scores 0%. All-Pass (secondary): 100% only if every check passes, 0% otherwise.' Two-hour time limit per task, over time scores zero.
scorer: 'All responses are graded by a three-judge LLM jury consisting of three frontier models: GPT-5.4, Gemini-3.1-Pro, and Claude Sonnet 4.6.' No scorer code in the public repo (no judge prompts, no aggregation code). Grading runs through the gated Vals platform. How the jury votes are combined is not documented on the page (null).

'Private Validation (450 samples available for license) ... Interested parties are encouraged to contact us directly for access.' Price and terms not public.
'Test (450 samples) ... The Test set will remain private. All results reported on this page are based solely on the Test set'.

claim_checks.note: Severity-weighted, dealbreaker-gated. The public rubric encodes severity and `category: must_pass`. That must_pass == dealbreaker is my inference, the page never names the field.

notes: README lists 5 tools and omits calculator, the vals.ai page says six tools, the code defines 7 Tool classes including submit_final_result.
Makefile sets PYTHON_VERSION ?= 3.11 but pyproject.toml has requires-python >=3.12. `make install` may fail as written, use `make install PYTHON_VERSION=3.12`. Not executed, so unverified.

You can run the agent locally on the 27 public questions without platform access, but you would have to write your own jury scorer from the rubric JSON, and it would not be the official score.

name: Invoice Sandbox Benchmark
license_note: No LICENSE file and GitHub reports license=null. Legally that is all rights reserved, no reuse grant. README only says 'All names, invoices, emails, and amounts are synthetic.'
access: public GitHub repo, not archived, 1 star, single day of history (created and last pushed 2026-06-10)
agent_visible_inputs: Only `runs/<run-id>/workspace`, which reset_env.py creates as a straight copy of gold_master/: invoices/*.pdf, email_archive/eml/*.eml + support_inbox.mbox, bank_exports/deposits_2025_q4.csv, crm/customer_master.csv, operations/ar_aging_snapshot.csv, operations/service_catalog.csv, notes/controller_close_notes.txt
private_material: answer_key/customer_totals.csv (customer_id, customer_name, valid_invoice_count, gross_invoice_spend_usd, credit_memo_total_usd, net_spend_usd)
answer_key/invoices.csv (per-document status, policy, canonical_id, net_spend_effect_usd, hidden_flags)
answer_key/traps.json
answer_key/manifest.json
scripts/ (README says keep private: generate_fixture.py contains the seed and all trap logic, score_submission.py reads the key)
native_metric: score_submission.py prints customers_scored, customers_exact, customer_accuracy (= exact / 18), total_absolute_error_usd, missing_customers, unexpected_customers. Only `net_spend_usd` per customer_id is compared, default tolerance 0.01 USD absolute (`--tolerance`). net_spend_usd = included valid invoices - credit memos.
scorer: scripts/score_submission.py (stdlib only). Usage: python scripts/score_submission.py path\to\submission.csv [--tolerance 0.01]
expected_agent_output: A CSV with at least columns `customer_id` and `net_spend_usd` (money parsed after stripping $ and commas). README's fuller 'primary expected output' is customer-level gross valid invoice spend, credit memo total, net spend, valid invoice count, and a list of excluded or suspicious documents with reasons, but none of those extra fields are machine-scored.
submission_rules: None. Local scoring only, no leaderboard.

claim_checks.claim: README lists CLI commands, agent output format, answer key location, scorer

claim_checks.note: answer_key/manifest.json says pdf_count 112 and the git tree has 112 PDFs under gold_master/invoices. README is stale by 2.

notes: NAMING TRAP for the registry: `gold_master/` is the agent-visible fixture, NOT gold answers. The gold answers are in `answer_key/`.
Commands are documented in PowerShell blocks with Windows path separators, but they are plain python and the scripts use pathlib.

gold_master is committed, so generate_fixture.py --clean is optional. Whether regenerating reproduces the committed files byte for byte (manifest has generated_at_utc) is unverified, I ran nothing. If you regenerate, answer_key is regenerated too.
Some trap hints are visible in workspace filenames by design, e.g. INV-2025-1013_duplicate_scan_from_email.pdf and 999_reconciliation_warning.eml.
requirements.txt (reportlab>=4.0, pillow>=10.0) is only needed for fixture generation, scoring is stdlib.
Isolation is on you: the workspace lives inside the repo at runs/<id>/workspace, so an agent with parent-directory access can read ../../answer_key. Copy the workspace out or mount it alone.
